clue.text: Reveals another sound that goes on and on

indicators.note: another version of the word Reveals is wanted, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ting is a light ringing sound

explanation.surface: Someone keeps disclosing yet another noise that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' asks for a different arrangement of REVEALS, giving EVERLAS; TING, a ringing sound, completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless or perpetual is described as never ceasing, going on and on.

clue.text: Star name of one who won't eat meat

parts.note: Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: The name of a celebrity who refuses meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict vegetarian avoids all animal products, meat included.

clue.text: Fall back into another error?

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, giving another go at something
a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: Someone slides back into making yet another mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning reading: a RE-LAPSE is another lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to regress or sink back into a former state, such as illness or a bad habit.

clue.text: Certainly not getting any younger

parts.note: a wry way of describing anyone whose years keep piling up, read straight as a description of growing old

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about the passing years.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older is the plain opposite of becoming younger.

clue.text: Volunteers on deck arranged to have it attached

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of deck are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Volunteers on a ship's deck fix something in place.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve; 'arranged' is the anagram signal for the ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacked on is fastened or added on, often as an afterthought.

clue.text: Puzzle no more

explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus is to baffle or perplex someone; the Latin non plus means literally not further, a state of having nowhere else to go.

clue.text: Important reports but not inside information

definitions.text: Important reports but not inside information

parts.words: Important reports but not inside information
parts.note: inside information sounds like secret knowledge, but here it means stories printed on the inner pages rather than the very first one of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Major stories that are not insider secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Headline stories are the big items given the prominent opening page of a newspaper.

clue.text: Composition from speaker number ten, it appears

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
the figures 1 and 0 of ten look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A piece of music from the man speaking at Number Ten, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten suggests Downing Street, the British prime minister's residence; here it is just the numeral 10, read as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for voices and orchestra, a type of composition.

clue.text: Prostrate after mishap and likely to get hurt

indicators.note: after places the word for prostrate behind the word for mishap

parts.note: an accident is a mishap
prostrate means lying face down, prone

explanation.surface: Someone lies flat after a mishap and seems liable to injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps having mishaps is clumsy and liable to injury.

clue.text: Concerning young lady, some say, not common

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: some people pronounce the word for a young lady in this clipped way

parts.note: a girl is a young lady

explanation.surface: A remark about a young woman who is said to be rather posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' points to a way of pronouncing GIRL, as GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal or stately bearing is the opposite of common or vulgar.

clue.text: Odd person deviating from normal conduct

explanation.surface: A strange individual who behaves unconventionally.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball is a person whose behaviour departs from the conventional, the same word serving as noun and adjective.

clue.text: A neat sum

parts.note: a sum looks like a tidy amount of money, alluding to the old saying about being as neat or right as a certain old coin worth nine pennies

explanation.surface: A tidy amount of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'neat as ninepence' is an old British saying; pre-decimal Britain had pence in its coinage, so this sum was a real amount.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount of nine old pennies figures in the old saying meaning very tidy.

clue.text: I halt movement using a heavy stick

indicators.note: movement means the letters of I halt are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone stops moving, wielding a heavy club.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a long iron-bound bamboo club used by police in South Asia.

clue.text: Term of affection father gives to his favourite

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Dad calls his favourite child by a loving nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A fond name for a small child or loved one, like darling.

clue.text: Window overlooking the sea

parts.note: a sea-view sounds like a room in a hotel, but the round opening meant is in a ship's side

explanation.surface: A room with a sea view.
explanation.definitionFit: A round opening in a ship's hull gives a view of the water outside.

clue.text: Study new verse about old-fashioned jam

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn

indicators.note: new means a fresh arrangement of the letters of verse

explanation.surface: Read a new poem about traditional preserves.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an archaic verb for studying; 'new' signals the anagram of the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserve of fruit boiled with sugar; the word for this is now rather dated.

clue.text: Adapt again having perused barely a moment ago

parts.note: perused means read
just means barely and also a moment ago

explanation.surface: Someone changes a plan after reading it only seconds earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: To make fresh small changes so something suits once more, a repeated adjustment.

clue.text: Got at red revolutionary and strangled him?

indicators.note: revolutionary means the letters of Got at red are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone attacked a communist and throttled him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' and 'revolutionary' paint a political surface; 'revolutionary' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Garrotting is killing by throttling with a cord or wire.

clue.text: Strengthen temper

explanation.definitionFit: To make harder or more resilient; to temper steel is to harden it by heat treatment.

clue.text: Nearly all the biggest part, nearly all

indicators.note: nearly means the word all loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
most means the greater or biggest part

explanation.surface: A repetitive stab at saying nearly the whole lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue bookends itself: 'Nearly' clips the first 'all', and 'nearly' at the end defines the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Two synonyms for very nearly, all but.

clue.text: Left with each fellow allowed to produce a booklet

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: Each departing fellow is permitted to publish a pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small printed pamphlet, usually handed out free.

clue.text: In the middle of maids dancing on the square

indicators.note: dancing means the letters of maids jig into a new order

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can stand for square

explanation.surface: Surrounded by maids dancing in the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' signals the anagram; T stands for square because of the T-square used in technical drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst means among or surrounded by, at the centre of things.

clue.text: Bird backing rugby leader

indicators.note: backing means the word for a bird is read in reverse

parts.note: a hen is a bird
RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A bird supporting the captain of a rugby team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rugby leader' looks like a captain; 'leader' alone is the definition, India's first prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru led India as its first prime minister after independence.

clue.text: Humble with our manner towards another

parts.note: to humble someone is to demean them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being humbled alters how we behave to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing and behaviour shown to others is one's conduct.

clue.text: Some cloak entirely made of wood!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cloak made entirely of timber, absurdly.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaken describes something built from the timber of the oak tree.

clue.text: Run back and harass the beast

indicators.note: back means the word for run is read in reverse

parts.note: to run is to flow, as water does
to hound is to harass

explanation.surface: Run back and pester the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolfhound is a large hunting dog, a beast in the loose sense.

clue.text: Compare with link 'e forged

indicators.note: forged means the letters of link 'e are hammered into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone says he made a chain link, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them.

clue.text: Setting up a foundation, nothing less grand

indicators.note: less means the following item is removed from the word for foundation

parts.note: an institution is a foundation, such as a charity
O looks like zero, nothing
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Establishing a charitable foundation with nothing left over but a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes O (nothing) from INSTITUTION, leaving INSTITUTIN, then G is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Instituting is establishing or founding something.
